Stepwise selection with AIC or BIC

select_stepwise_ic.Rd

Forward, backward or bidirectional stepwise selection via MASS::stepAIC(). Predictors are standardized first; see tidy.selector().

Usage

select_stepwise_ic(
  formula,
  data,
  family = c("gaussian", "binomial"),
  select_factors_together = FALSE,
  penalty = c("AIC", "BIC"),
  direction = c("forward", "backward", "both"),
  criterion = c("deviance", "cp"),
  sigma = NULL,
  trace = 0,
  fitted_selector = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula

a model formula, as for lm(). It may include interactions (x * z) and in-formula transformations (log(x), poly(x, 2)); factor, logical and character predictors are treatment-coded. Ordered factors and missing values are not supported. See tidy.selector() for how the columns are standardized and named.

data

a data frame

family

outcome distributional family: "gaussian" or "binomial" ("poisson" is not yet supported)

select_factors_together

should the dummy columns of a factor enter or leave the model together?

penalty

"AIC" (default) or "BIC"

direction

the search direction: "forward" (default), "backward" or "both"

criterion

which form of the information criterion to minimize:

  • "deviance" (default): n * log(RSS / n) + k * df, as in MASS::stepAIC().

  • "cp": the Mallows-Cp form RSS + k * sigma^2 * df, which is what selectiveInference conditions on.

Here k = 2 for AIC and log(n) for BIC.

The two can stop at different steps. When they do, infer_selective() falls back from conditioning on the IC stopping rule (type = "aic") to conditioning on a fixed number of steps (type = "active"), which treats the number of selected terms as fixed in advance; the effect of this seems to be minor. "cp" avoids the fallback. It requires family = "gaussian", direction = "forward" and select_factors_together = FALSE.

sigma

residual standard deviation defining the criterion = "cp" penalty. Ignored when criterion = "deviance". When NULL the same rule selectiveInference::fsInf() uses is applied.

trace

passed to MASS::stepAIC()

fitted_selector

a previously fit selector, used by reselect()

...

additional arguments passed to MASS::stepAIC()

Value

a selector; see tidy.selector(). Its default inference method is infer_boot().
